poiNAU-desc:
The North American Union is a country in name far more than in practice. Central, the government that emerged from the Siege of Washington in 2084, still speaks for the Union abroad, signs its treaties and holds its seat among the nations. At home, its authority barely reaches past its own district. The rest of the Union is carved into numbered Districts, each with its own {{poiNAU026|cliques}}, militaries and loyalties. On paper they all belong to {{poiNAU030|a Greater American Identity}} that also embraces Canada and Mexico. In practice most of them pay Central {{poiNAU002|nothing beyond lip service}}.

Central's great rival is ARC, the American Reclamation Corporation. It began as a government contractor, sent in to rescue and resettle populations after {{poiNAU009|the disasters}} that followed the Great Mistake. Over the decades that work earned it the loyalty, the capital and the checkpoints that Central never managed to keep. Today some Districts answer to Central, {{poiNAU011|some to ARC}}, some to {{poiNAU005|both at once}}, and {{poiNAU015|some to neither}}. Where ARC governs, it governs like a company: with {{poiNAU017|oversight boards}}, {{poiNAU022|research mandates}} and a close eye on the quarterly returns of rejuvenation technology.

{{poiNAU031|Older powers}} linger beneath both. {{poiNAU007|The United Nations}} clings to life in {{poiNAU025|New England}}, the remnants of the pre-war warlords and {{poiNAU004|the Chrysalids}} still prowl the West, and everywhere there are tribes, {{poiNAU003|raiders}} and {{poiNAU010|refugee towns}} that predate the Union and expect to outlast it. Few of them recognize anyone's right to rule.

Now the Union faces a crisis of succession. President Cygan will not seek another term, and the {{poiNAU012|Central Council}}, an unofficial sea of politicians, lobbyists, officers and spies, {{poiNAU013|must choose his successor}}. {{poiNAU001|The Joint Chiefs}} will have the last word. {{poiNAU014|Whoever wins}} inherits a Union held together by whoever is strongest in the room, and in the year 2200 nobody is quite sure who that is.
poiNAU001-desc: After the Siege of Washington in 2084, where the military forced the pre-Mistake government into exile in order to break the political deadlock that only exacerbated the chaos gripping the country from disasters and militia violence, the Central government was never truly able to fulfill their promise of restoring the government. Even though all three of the pre-Mistake branches are present, it's only the Executive that has any practical ability to pass policy, and even they are beholden to the Joint Chiefs. This has led to the military often being described as The Fourth Branch—mostly by anti-Central factions lambasting it as a glorified military dictatorship, but occasionally by members of the Central military who feel they deserve the political influence they wield for protecting democracy.
poiNAU002-desc: While the many Districts disagree, often violently, they have one agreement in common; Central is the worst. Even citizens living within the region the Central government directly controls hate them, to the point that the military police cannot contain the rising protest movements. Others have found comfort instead in the sermons of {{poiNAU018|Miriam Godwinson}}, the Psych Chaplain whose Evangelical Fire has followers even inside Central's own forces. Whoever the Central Council appoints as President, they will need to deal with the protestors... one way, or another.
poiNAU003-desc: The provinces once known as California are fried. Just like its East Coast counterpart, the land is heavily flooded and has a bloody history of anarchy. The few who remain live their lives as raiders, pillaging long-abandoned homes and farms in a never-ending search for food. Scars from meltdowns and chemical warfare still plague the air. The only order left is the kind that is paid for: the Spartanists of {{poiNAU023|Corazon Santiago}} clear out bandit hideouts in return for the settlements' protection tribute.
poiNAU004-desc: District 2 has been fighting the subversive Chrysalids for some time now. As the last remnants of pre-war warlords, the enigmatic {{poiNAU029|Silk Path}} has continued to be a thorn in the side of both Central and ARC. District 2's officers are tasked with cleansing the District of the subversives… but may have other plans waiting in store.
poiNAU005-desc:
District 2 is ruled by two organizations simultaneously.

The first is the ARC Delegation, led by Vice President {{poiNAU016|Antony Beaton}} of Reclamation Cascadia. Although far away from home, this clique has managed to secure a support base among the District's affluent citizenry. Due to its mountainous nature, old Cascadia has escaped the worst of the Great Mistake, which has allowed it to keep a sizable middle class, which is all too eager to support Beaton's promises of extended life.

The other faction, led by Relief Officer {{poiNAU024|Haven Barnett}}, is the Central Delegation. While it draws popular backing from the poorer Southern parts, it has roots in the upper classes as well. Though less radical than her ARC counterpart, Barnett also seeks the elusive goal of extended life.

For now, the two factions are united in the struggle against the Western warlord. But as victory draws closer, the cracks deepen, and the whole structure can come crashing down...
poiNAU006-desc: The land once known as the East Coast is dead and buried under the sea. Following the Great Mistake, the entire populations of New York, Boston, and other ancient metropoli fled for the Midwest. As expected, the unstable Federal government was unable to deal with mass migration and buckled in the 2nd American Civil War. Famine set in. Families turned into gangs and friends killed friends just for a slice of meat. So it continues to this day. The East Coast is in complete anarchy. The only authority comes from ARC's enforcers, who have fortified checkpoints and refugee camps, bringing some semblance of order to the wastes.
poiNAU007-desc:
Were a person to travel back to the 21st century and question its inhabitants as to the projected situation of the United Nations two hundred years forward, few would have guessed that the once global organization would be hanging on to dear life in some backwater. But this is indeed the case, and Earth's finest have been stranded in New England for centuries. Children have heard stories of wars and the apocalypse from their soldier-parents, grown into adults and died while still wearing the UN insignia.

The dream of a united Earth lives on, fueled by loss and regret. Perhaps the Coasts have nothing left to lose, or perhaps, in some rusted half-sunk home is a new generation, born into poverty but kept alive by stories of a wonderful world that awaits just beyond the horizon...
poiNAU008-desc:
During the Great Mistake, many of old America's finest fled to the Great Lakes to seek shelter from the anarchy and floods that dominated the coasts. They brought with them vast capital, giving the dying Rust Belt quick injections of cold cash and propelling the Midwest to new heights.

Today, the Great Lakes lay claim to what little remains of America's vestigial wealth. The Greater Chicago Area boasts one of the highest standards of living in the world, while Detroit is widely considered to be the manufacturing capital of the continent. Corporations can pursue their interests in peace, free from unnecessary government intervention and regulations. However, its prosperity may attract unwanted visitors, or even a full invasion...
poiNAU009-desc: Following the collapse of civilization on the North American continent during the latter half of the 21st century, a Great Migration began. Millions fled the coasts in panic, bringing with them children, the old, the crippled. New Englanders and Yankees settled across Pennsylvania at first, but gang tensions and famines forced another migration further West. Even today, {{poiNAU032|Michigan}} and other Eastern states have to deal with hundreds of refugee towns. Boys have grown into men and bit the dust in these settlements, and even lowlifes call the refugee camps a cesspit. Now that tensions are rising across Central's loose domain, {{poiNAU008|Chicago}} finds itself in the position of rare governmental unity, and can take action as needed.
poiNAU010-desc: The local population of this District is in a constant state of flux. Refugees from Louisiana still inhabit the Eastern coast, but regularly undergo famine as the fishing industry declines. Meanwhile, bandits and tribes from Mexico travel Northwards annually in search of more suitable climates. The recent uprising in Southern Mexico has further fueled this migration, and thousands are making their way through the border. This issue is continually destabilizing District 6 and will lend much political capital to whoever manages to resolve it.
poiNAU011-desc: District 6 is currently divided between ARC and Central loyalists. The former, led by Vice President {{poiNAU020|Suzanne Fielding}} herself, consists primarily of middle-class supporters and those who stand to benefit by extensive reclamation projects along the Eastern coast. On the other end, Central loyalists are led by Axton Barron, the former representative of District 6 before his ostracization from politics in the 80s. Now, having recovered much of his political capital, Barron has returned to re-secure Texas in the name of Central. His support is primarily drawn from rich elites and power brokers who have a vested interest in attaining Central relief aid.
poiNAU012-desc:
In the pre-Mistake era, a phrase often associated with the old United States was It can't happen here. This sentiment was for a multitude of scenarios the citizens felt would only be plausible in elaborate works of fiction; disastrous weather tearing down entire cities, American citizens killing each other in the streets, the White House and Capitol Building being stormed by soldiers to establish martial law. Then when the Great Mistake choked the skies with ash, rising tides swallowed entire states whole, militias and gangs waged violence from coast-to-coast, and the military launched the Siege of Washington in 2084, almost every concept that Americans believed couldn't happen, did happen.

While the Central government still has vestiges of the pre-Mistake branches of government, and had theoretically shed the pre-Mistake jingoism by adopting Canada and Mexico in a Greater American Identity, the national rebirth via military coup has made the Legislative and Judiciary branches rife with corruption and Machiavellian power schemes at best, and glorified rubber stamps for the President and Joint Chiefs at worst. The Executive branch, despite having the best security on the continent, routinely had their administrations prematurely ended by assassination, leading many to believe even they are but a puppet to the military, and those who don't follow the whims of their generals will have their own security turn on them like the Praetorians of Imperial Rome. Of course, how much of this is truth, and how much is anti-Central conspiracy theory, is ill-defined.

With President Cygan having finished his term in office, citing health concerns as the reason he won't run for reelection, the question of who will lead the Central government is once again open to debate. The ongoing crisis has long since thrown any elections from the common citizenry out the window, most especially after the Districts, while in theory still under Central administration, in practice became effectively independent nation-states with little loyalty paid to Central beyond the bare minimum of lip service. Thus, the Central Council—the unofficial name for the roiling sea of politicians, lobbyists, officers and spies feuding for power—is convening to select a new President, and perhaps implement some broader government reforms to salvage what little control it has left.

This could be the opportunity for the spark of democracy to reignite... or be snuffed out, once and for all.
poiNAU013-desc:
As the leader of the Patriot Party, Luis Segerra Reyes was widely known to be President Cygan’s de facto successor after the latter declined to run for reelection. Reyes worked in the Central District as its ruling Governor, despite having only earned his citizenship status from when Central made its abortive attempt to take Mexico in the 2170s. Fiercely loyal to his newfound country, Reyes believes that the Central District represents the true legitimate authority in North America, and should be developed as the supreme capital of a unified continent.

During his time as governor, Reyes has obtained significant influence among Central’s political and military elites. He has also attracted widespread popularity in the general public, who are taken in by his restorationist rhetoric and self-styled image as the only leader strong enough to lead their decaying nation back to its former glory. With the power of Central behind him, Reyes is determined to return America to its superpower status, no matter the cost.
poiNAU014-desc:
Emerging as a dark horse in the race to replace Cygan, Wesley Forrest and his Elysium Party have managed to secure a surprising amount of support in the labyrinthine oligarchy of the Central Council. One of the youngest party leaders in Central’s history, Forrest grew up as part of the privileged upper class that had access to pre-Mistake history, culture, and even samples of preserved flora and fauna. More idealistic than past candidates, he wishes to restore democratic institutions in the Central government and take decisive action to regenerate America’s fading biospheres.

This platform has earned him broad approval of the masses, though it was much more pragmatic political maneuvering that carried the Elysium Party to prominence. Even so, Forrest’s ascension has made him many outspoken enemies within Central’s assorted internal cliques. Many within the Council suspect that Forrest is being puppeted by the Joint Chiefs to shore up crumbling public support and ecological conditions, and that he will be disposed of should any of his proposed reforms truly threaten their power. His own followers remain hopeful that he will yet succeed, even if it means fighting for the very soul of the NAU.
poiNAU015-desc:
District 1 has no governing body or civilization. There are no urban cities, American suburbs, or even sustainable farms. The District's inhabitants are forced to either hunt increasingly scarce prey, vegetation, or, in more extreme instances, each other. As the District is incapable of producing its own supplies, much less its own weapons, it relies on occasional Central shipments.

Thus, as time has passed, Central has tightened its grip on the District. All ammunition inflow is possible solely through Central's approval. This new power has therefore made many successful attempts at playing the local tribes against one another. The cliques are taking over one another, completely oblivious to their position on Central's chopping block. However, immediate reconstruction of social order in District 1 is impossible. The land is ruined by poisonous gases released by warlords over the decades. Irradiated ruins still dot the plains and hills. And the survivors keep fighting...
poiNAU016-desc:
Antony Beaton is the regional Vice President of ARC Reclamation Projects in Cascadia. Beaton began his career in 2182 as a clerk in Central government departments before moving to the East Coast in search of wider opportunities. His finances ran dry and he had to take refuge in an ARC encampment near New England. There Beaton partook in several skirmishes with raiders before being discharged from the city militias due to a festering leg wound. He would spend the next 3 years in a research hospital, where he was spared from irreparable status by undergoing a miraculous recovery.

Still recovering, Antony Beaton enlisted in the hospital staff and began a career as a research scientist. He proved his worth many times over by assisting hundreds of patients, which prompted the head doctor to recommend Beaton to his superiors in ARC itself. Beaton spent the following years studying medicine and showed an extreme interest in rejuvenation technology. He ascended the ranks at a lightning speed and was eventually assigned to lead an ARC expedition into District 2, in the hopes of flipping it to ARC's side. The Cascadian wilderness allowed Beaton to exercise his strong leadership and strategic skills. Now, Beaton has become somewhat enchanted by the enemy he is facing, the Silk Path. He makes vague promises of eternal life to his closest followers and not even ARC believes that he is a completely loyal asset anymore. However, Beaton has organized a large support base and is unlikely to stop his search.
poiNAU017-desc:
The ARC Oversight Board is a ruling council composed of 20 members, 18 of whom are direct corporate representatives from ARC itself. Assigned to the District with the stated goal of maintaining order and reviving civilization, the Board's members have elected to build up their strength by going on vacations and purchasing the newest augmentations. ARC would do something about this insubordination, but is too preoccupied with global concerns. The Board controls the only organized military force in the District, the 68th and 45th ARC Peacekeeping Divisions.

While opposed at nearly every opportunity by local interest groups and the United Nations, the Oversight Board's power is near total. The Board commands full respect in the cities by controlling their water flow and ration intakes. While dissent is theoretically meant to be dealt with swiftly, the Board has been accused of neglecting its duties and allowing the raiders to grow out of control.
poiNAU018-desc:
Miriam Godwinson was born in what was once Georgia, 2146. Her father was a high-ranking minister in the Evangelical Fire, one of the apocalyptic sects that appeared in local communities after the turn of the century. Baptized in River of Fire at age 7, she attended a series of religious schools, culminating in a degree in theology from the College of the Covenant and a doctorate in psychology from Newland University. By the time Godwinson began her own ministry, the Evangelical Fire was the largest Christian denomination in her home region. By the age of 26, she was the ranking Psych Priest of the Heavenly Diocese, third most senior member of the sect. In 2174, she volunteered to serve with Central Reintegration Forces sent to the North. Appointed Central District Honorary Psych Chaplain, she proved to be a talented military psychologist, but at the same time, her religious ministry to the desperate people of the region backfired.

Upon returning to the South, millions hailed her as a kind of messiah (the Prophet Phenomenon often coinciding with post-Mistake madness), forcing Central to release her from service before her presence could further inflame local religious mania. Authorities were reluctant to have such a controversial figure in a high leadership position in the District, but political pressure from the communities for the reconciling of the secular and the spiritual forced them to consider her for the position of Psych Chaplain. Her undeniable talent for that role eventually won her the appointment. Miriam is a relic of a different age. She values order and morality, and is always at odds with the march of progress. Humanity is but a child in her eyes, running from home into the great unknown.
poiNAU019-desc: The Great Lakes Committee is a council of local leaders, career politicians, and corporate representatives tasked with the preservation of order and steady growth in {{poiNAU008|the Great Lakes District}}. Although initially appointed by Central in the aftermath of the 3rd American Civil War, the Committee now functions as an independent political entity. Its members are often seen as ineffectual by the wider public, but without proper elections, things are unlikely to change. Its one undisputed success is the body it created to deal with the refugees in the East, the {{poiNAU032|Settlement and Survival Committee}}, which has since grown strong enough to worry Chicago.
poiNAU020-desc: Suzanne Fielding was born the eldest of three daughters to a Mexican-born mother, and an African-American father in April, 2161. Growing up close to the Gulf Coast of Texas, she helped her father manage the three hardware stores he owned in the state—the fruits of the Central government's attempts to revitalize the region's economy after the 3rd American Civil War's so-called War of Unification. Although Central would abandon direct control of District 6 along with much of the country, Fielding exploited what opportunity was given by graduating from San Antonio's Trinity University with a double Majors in Accounting and Economics. Since then, she has made considerable progress in building a support base stretching from her native Texas to ARC itself.
poiNAU021-desc:
Spencer Morgan began his career as an enlistee in the Central army during the early days of the 3rd Civil War. He distinguished himself by leading the famous Littletown Raid, in which he, a dozen footmen and a decrepit walker managed to break through warlord defenses and occupy Littletown, a major stronghold in the Rocky Mountains. This victory paved the way for Central domination over transportation in the mountain ranges, allowing it to operate across multiple fronts at lightning speeds. Major Morgan went on to participate in critical clashes in California and garnered much fame for his argument against the utilization of nuclear weapons against warlords there. Eventually a colonel and then a general, Spencer Morgan finished his military career at the age of 32 when he successfully pacified the warlord Dangerman in the Midwest.

For his service, General Morgan was granted {{poiNAU026|authority over District 7}}. Exchanging the sword for the pen, Morgan proved himself a capable administrator and negotiator. He signed treaties with the local tribes and gangs, bringing much needed order to District 7. His rule saw the creation of entire cities, the resettlement of abandoned lands, and the establishment of a culture fluent in politics. Now an old man, General Morgan has mostly withdrawn from the public sphere. He spends his days secluded in his forest cabin, which has allowed bandits to resurface on the periphery. His supporters have begun to forget the man's contributions and some wonder just how strong his grip over District 7 really is.
poiNAU022-desc: There are many words that have been used to describe ARC's Chief Research Officer Gabriel Ivanov. Ambitious. Quirky. Antisocial. Sociopathic. Psychopathic. However, despite having almost every adjective that has existed in the English language—and a multitude of foreign language adjectives with no real equivalent in English—being used to describe Ivanov—by his admirers, his detractors, and even by himself—one word that cannot be said of him at any time is being complacent. Having effectively turned the entirety of District 8 into a glorified ARC research facility, the only real threat to Ivanov's authority is the rising sentiment of Canadian separatism that wants to stop the Firaxite Man from making their homeland his personal petri dish.
poiNAU023-desc:
Corazon Santiago was born in District 1 in 2159 to a family of pirates from Puerto Rico. While she was still young her family fled to Central, where she was orphaned in the riots of 2165. She took her younger siblings and joined a survivalist street gang, the Jade Falcons. She survived the experience. When she reappeared in District 1, her siblings had vanished. Santiago never speaks of them, and their fate is unknown.

In old California she served in a settlement security force, the Red Panthers, then joined the City Guard of Wayward Harbor, one of the District's largest villages, and distinguished herself as a battalion commander when a warlord attacked the town. The fame it brought set her on the path to founding the Spartanists, a selective order of survivalists who make their living in old California by destroying bandit hideouts and collecting protection tribute from the settlements.

Disciplined, agile and able to thrive anywhere, she is regarded as an exceptional leader. She is adaptable, aggressive, proud and extremely tenacious, and her personality is one of icy self-control over volcanic rage, the legacy of a tormented childhood. She will stop at nothing to ensure her own survival and that of her followers. In the end, she means to make herself absolute ruler of old America.
poiNAU024-desc:
The daughter of a prominent Central statesman, Haven Barnett has lived her whole life in the Rocky Mountains. Given everything and wasting nothing, she graduated as valedictorian, won three pan-American gold medals in skiing, and rose almost at once to high status, taking over her late father's position. Her career eclipsed everything else. She is unmarried and childless, and could not care less.

In 2193 she became regional representative of Lesser Central, a bold move that left her rivals in the dust and set them plotting. Distracted by riots and by her public image, she was suddenly ousted on corruption charges. Her money bought good lawyers and she kept her position, if not her reputation. Fearing for her safety and sensing another plot, she accepted a reassignment to District 2 as Relief Officer, with an explicit goal, to crush the last pre-war warlord there, and a secret one: to isolate and defeat the ARC expedition beside her.

She is no scientist, but she has realised what she may be sitting on. The District's scientists and facilities are all too suited to the search for immortality, the cure for aging.
poiNAU025-desc:
Pravin Lal was born in New England in 2166, to a long line of UN Peacekeepers. He studied philosophy and medicine in Arcopolis, then returned to the countryside to work as a thoracic surgeon. When ARC expanded into New England, his selfless devotion to victims of radiation burns won him wide acclaim, and his experience of the horrors of war led him into UN office. He served for many months in the village of I Made It, rose to Assistant Director of the regional office, and in the divisions that followed the 3rd Civil War proved himself a capable commander against raiders.

His wife, Pria, was mortally wounded in a firefight during Young Oyster's Raid. Rumour says he preserved a piece of her DNA. Little else about her, or about Lal's past with her, is public.

Lal is a strong idealist, the best of what remains of Earth's world community. He seeks to de-escalate conflict and build harmony, and he performs well under extreme pressure: .87 on the Atherholt Trauma Function Test, recovery score moderate. A democrat and a pragmatist by nature, he will follow those ideals as far as he possibly can.
poiNAU026-desc:
District 7 is at war, an invisible war fought in people's minds. The Midwest was relatively spared by the Great Mistake and too large to bear the full scars of the Civil Wars and the anarchy, and its people have reached a prosperity rarely seen on the continent. Local businesses flourish despite the government's tight grip on the market, a computer-assisted administration keeps the factories and farms efficient, and even the poor can live without fear of bandits or famine. That semblance of the old world has produced something rarer still: a real middle and upper class, and a politicized public.

Two men compete for the District. One is {{poiNAU021|Spencer Morgan}}, the old general and master administrator who conquered the Midwest in the 3rd Civil War and watched it prosper. The other is the man Morgan's supporters call a usurper: ARC's representative, {{poiNAU027|Jensen Laneman}}. Both believe in the past, a better past, but as their followers brawl in the streets and make ever larger promises, the gap between them only grows. Some major upset is coming. The only question is who will come out on top.
poiNAU027-desc:
If there is one thing Colonel Jensen Laneman clings to more than his sidearm, it is his heritage. When the Federal government let America fall into chaos during the Great Mistake, his great-grandfather was among the soldiers who stormed Capitol Hill. When Central withdrew to Denver after {{poiNAU006|the East Coast}} sank into the sea, his grandfather put on a uniform as soon as he was old enough to enlist. When Central launched the War of Unification, Jensen and his father fought in it together, his father as a senior officer and Jensen as a young frontline recruit. And when Central let the country slip through its fingers rather than tighten its grip, Jensen resigned in disgust.

He spent the years that followed as a wandering mercenary, joining any backwoods militia willing to fight the "spineless Centrists". He became a thorn in the side of Central-aligned warlords and a near-legendary exterminator of urban gangs and rival militias, with particular brutality reserved for self-proclaimed socialists. ARC found his skills too useful to ignore. The Corporation quietly rewrote his record, pulled him out of a foxhole in the Cascadian forest and installed him in a fortified office complex in what was once New Jersey, at the head of its private military contractors.

Laneman took the chance to command a real army, but he has never accepted ARC's idea of America: a gaggle of business suits and media brats willing to make any transaction, however degrading, while an "invisible hand" conducts the bloated corporate orchestra. His America would be one of discipline and order, with a Supreme Executive above a cowed legislature and judiciary, every citizen ready to fight and bleed, every child taught the true history of the nation, and every foreigner made to serve or cast out. Not a union of the continent, but the United States of centuries past, with Canada and Mexico beneath it. For now he takes ARC's pay and follows ARC's orders. Those who know him say it is a matter of when, not if.
poiNAU028-desc:
An enigma. A philosopher. A saviour. A fleeting memory of the old world. These are some of the words used to describe John Doe, the most mysterious man in North America.

He first appears in official records in 2148, when a Central probe team reported that he had gathered a small following of mercenaries in Oregon. After a brief firefight he was captured and imprisoned with other petty warlords. The guards noted that he was already an ancient man, likely in his eighties. No fingerprints could be taken because of his prosthetic hands, and the prison was abandoned before anyone could study him further. He walked out and slipped into obscurity.

He resurfaced in 2161 at the head of a small army of fanatics, his face hidden behind an esoteric iron mask. When Central launched its Northern Campaign in 2166, he was one of many warlords who resisted, and the greatest of them. But the years dragged on and the settlements fell one by one, and his realm, which once stretched from the Pacific to the Rockies, has shrunk to a few hideouts near the Seattle coast. Myths abound about who he really is, and one can only wonder what his ancient eyes have seen.
poiNAU029-desc:
{{poiNAU028|John Doe}} is waging a war on the past, and the past is winning. Once the greatest warlord realm of the American Anarchy in the Northwest, the Silk Path has been reduced to a rump state on the Seattle coast. The city itself is too broken to matter, but John Doe has made it ground zero for the extermination of the ancient culture that he says led the continent to ruin. There is sin in America's past, he teaches, and the only way to escape it is to extend the human lifespan.

The Silk Path is searching for a dream unseen, as old as Sumer: immortality. It rejects clinical immortality as a temporary answer to a far bigger problem, the sickness called aging. Its researchers have made modest advances in preserving the cohesion of tissue and mind, and some followers are said to have lived well past a century, but the treatment is extensive and restricted to John Doe's inner circle, the Chrysalids. Central and ARC have each sent a delegation to destroy it. Both, it is whispered, want its secrets more than its surrender.
poiNAU030-desc: Ever since the North American Union was formed after the 3rd Civil War, Canada has been treated, by foreigners and by much of its own population, as an integral part of the North American identity. In recent decades the old dream of a true, independent Canada has been reborn, largely through the efforts of one Thomas Woodman. Backed by rich and poor alike, all of them tired of ARC's extensive meddling in District affairs, many in old Canada now long for neutrality and a state of their own.
poiNAU031-desc:
The Newfoundland Naval Junta is the last remnant of the old Federal government of the United States. Its founders are long dead, but strict adherence to tradition has kept its culture almost unchanged for more than a century. Its people speak a dialect of their own, yet still consider themselves the true heirs of the United States, and of Canada. They do not recognise Central, and Central barely remembers them.

The Junta is built around its navy, and the navy is a museum. Years of poor maintenance and outside advances have left the once legendary US Fleet more fit for exhibition than for the high seas. The Junta lacks the materials and expertise to modernize it, and relies on its aircraft carriers and transports for living space and for trading for food.

Its President, Ulrik Svensgaard, was born in 2158 to a Newfoundland fisherman and a barkeep of Massachusetts descent, and broke with his family to join the Federal Navy. During the disastrous Battle of Baffin Bay in 2187 he rescued Flag Admiral Clarke and three other senior officers when the battle group's magazine exploded, and lost his left eye doing it. Offered any assignment he liked, he joked that he should be made President, since his leadership would not have sailed the navy bow-first into a massacre. He was promptly nominated by the Republican-Democrat Coalition. Rugged, self-reliant and touchy about his humble origins, he enjoys humbling those with grander pedigrees, but he is unfailingly polite, follows a kind of chivalric code with worthy enemies, and his word is his bond.
poiNAU032-desc:
In 2184 {{poiNAU019|the Great Lakes Committee}} founded the Settlement and Survival Committee to deal with the refugees in the East. Its members were drawn from corporate representatives and Strike Action leaders, and the strikers soon pushed the corporate members aside. To everyone's surprise, it worked: the Committee has resettled two million refugees in Michigan.

Many people owe their lives and their families' lives to its members, and they are ready to fight for them. Chicago grows more nervous of the Committee's influence by the year, and has begun looking for ways to quietly bring its leaders to heel. If it moves against them, the Committee is ready to claim the whole District in the name of its oppressed inhabitants.
